**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reserve status width while the project is loading**

At the supported 880 px minimum, this shrinkable `min_w_0` item only recovers enough space for the short offline label, but when `state()` is `None`, the additional padded `loading` element appended below consumes that space and can collapse the audio status back to zero width. Cover the real loading state in the compact-width test and reserve enough width for both indicators so startup does not reintroduce the original invisible-status failure.

The new case uses the actual constructor with stateNone and then consumes the real Service init event; it traverses both modes and880/881/960/1440/880. At880 status is61.5px whileNone and52px afterinit, each at least seven shaped characters50.75px. Existing project_tempo_input returns an empty element whileNone, which pays for the loading indicator. The return adds127test lines+2layout-neutral selectors, no sizing/content logic change or weakened old loaded/header oracle. Owner baseline initially failed only a missing selector after the width assertion already passed; that fixture error is retained. This resolves this specific loading hypothesis only, not the three newer Tab findings, full21, native fonts/physical display or merge clearance.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse Tab while arrangement pan owns the pointer**

When the workspace already has focus and the middle mouse button is holding an arrangement pan, this guard does not check `arrangement_pan`, so an unmodified Tab reaches `set_mode`; that method immediately cancels the pan and switches to Console before mouse-up. Treat the active pan like the other pointer gestures here so Tab cannot interrupt a captured timeline interaction.

This resolves the old held-pan finding only; three new pre-drag/menu/auxiliary capture findings on38c3 remain open, and full21/merge/native acceptance are separate.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard pre-drag pointer capture from Tab**

When the workspace has focus and the user holds the left mouse button on a clip or trim handle without yet crossing GPUI's drag threshold, only `pointer_down` is set; none of the active-drag checks here apply. Pressing Tab therefore switches to Console and unmounts the Arrangement element that owns the pending mouse-up, interrupting the captured interaction and potentially leaving `pointer_down` stale. Refuse the shortcut while `self.pointer_down.is_some()` as well.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse Tab while the device add menu is open**

When the workspace or a track header retains focus, clicking the device-panel add toggle only flips `device_panel.add_menu_open` and does not transfer focus (`device_panel.rs:1035-1038`). This guard handles the other popup states but omits that menu, so an unmodified Tab switches the workspace underneath the still-open device menu, contrary to the popup refusal contract in `docs/workspace-views.md:15-17`. Include the device add-menu state in this refusal.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block Tab during root-owned auxiliary drags**

The spectrum resize explicitly focuses `view.focus` when it begins, and device-chain overview/middle-button navigation can likewise start while that root focus remains, but neither `project_spectrum.resize` nor `device_panel.navigation.gesture` is covered here. Pressing Tab during either drag therefore changes workspaces; the device-navigation gesture is then canceled by its mode-sync path, while the spectrum resize continues over the newly switched view. Refuse Tab while either auxiliary pointer gesture is active, just as this guard already does for track resizing and Arrangement pan.
